raw_case_text:
An eight-month-old male child was brought by his parents in March 2006. The child had history of severe cough four months ago. Subsequently, he developed severe redness, watering and discharge in the right eye. His birth history revealed the child was a full-term normal delivery. There was no history of prenatal infection.
The child could not fixate or follow light with right eye whereas the left eye could fixate and follow the light. Right eye had conjunctival congestion, hazy cornea, an exudative mass in the anterior chamber. There was iris atrophy. Intraocular pressure was low in the right eye and normal in the left eye digitally. Fundus examination revealed no view in the right eye. Ultrasonography of the right eye showed vitreous cavity filled with moderately reflective dot echoes. There was no evidence of intraocular calcification. Choroid was grossly thickened (3.0 mm). No mass lesion or intraocular foreign body was seen. Axial length of the eyeball was 13.3 mm. Computerized tomography (CT) scan showed the right globe smaller in size with hyperdense vitreous without any calcification. Ultrasound and CT scan finding was suggestive of endophthalmitis in the right eye. Left eye was normal in all aspects.
As there was no visual potential, the right eye was enucleated. The globe measured 12 mm anteroposteriorly, 13 mm horizontally and 12 mm vertically. Cross-section showed shrunken globe with disorganized internal structure. Choroid and sclera were thickened. Optic nerve head could not be seen. Central callote was submitted for histopathological examination which showed a shrunken eyeball with thickening of the sclera [Fig. 1]. Sclera was infiltrated by inflammatory cells at the limbus, which was composed of lymphocytes and multiple histiocytes. Iris showed dense infiltration of lymphocytes, plasma cells and histiocytes. Lens was found to be shrunken with ruptured and folded lens capsule. Vitreous cavity showed extensive granulomatous inflammation with multiple Langerhan's giant cells. Retina could not be identified. Histopathological diagnosis was consistent with endophthalmitis. Special stains for the fungus by Gomori methenamine silver stain showed multiple septate fungi with 90  branching suggestive of Aspergillus species [Fig. 2]. The PCR-based RFLP for species identification revealed a cleavage pattern similar to Aspergillus fumigatus [Fig.3]. Child was examined by an internist. There was no evidence of systemic involvement due to Aspergillus infection. No risk factor, intake of oral steroid or immunosuppressive agent and malignancy was found. The child was doing well after six months.
DNA extraction from paraffin section was carried out by Qiamp kit (Qiagen, Germany) according to manufacturer's instructions.
PCR targeting ITS region: The PCR was carried out according to the method of Ferrer et al. For a 50 microl reaction, 8 microl of 200 microm dNTPs,5 microl of 10 X PCR buffer (5 mM MgCl2,500 mM KCl, 100 mM Tris Cl,0.01% gelatin), 6 microl of 10 mM MgCl2, 10 picomoles of forward primer, forward primer ITS1 - 5' tcc gta ggt gaa cct gcg g 3'and reverse primer ITS4 -5' tcc tcc gct tat tat gc 3' targeting ITS region. Ten microl of template DNA was used. Amplification was carried out in Perkin Elmer thermal cycler (Model 2700) consisting of initial denaturation at 95 C for 5 min followed by 35 cycles of denaturation at 95 C for 30 sec, annealing at 55 C for 1 min and final extension at 72 C for 1 min and a final extension of 72 C for 7 min. The amplification yielded 520 to 611 bp product according to different fungal species for ITS region.
The PCR-based RFLP was carried out on ITS amplified products using Hae -III enzyme. For a 25 microl reaction, 2.5 microl of Buffer (10 microl of amplified product) and 1 microl of Hae-III enzyme was added and incubated at 37 C for 3 h. The restriction enzyme digested products were resolved using 4% agarose gel electrophoresis.

subjective.chief_complaint: An 8-month-old male infant presented with severe redness, tearing, and discharge in the right eye along with inability to fixate or follow light.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The infant had a history of severe cough 4 months prior to presentation in March 2006, followed by progressive redness, watering, discharge, and loss of visual fixation in the right eye.
subjective.past_medical_history: Full-term normal vaginal delivery with no prenatal infection, systemic illness, malignancy, or exposure to corticosteroids or immunosuppressive agents.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for prior severe cough (4 months ago) and right eye redness, tearing, discharge, and vision loss; negative for systemic infection.

objective.physical_examination: Right eye could not fixate or follow light and showed conjunctival congestion, corneal haziness, an anterior chamber exudative mass, iris atrophy, low digital intraocular pressure, and no fundus view; the left eye fixed and followed light normally with normal IOP and exam. Pediatric internist examination found no systemic abnormalities.
objective.routine_investigations: B-scan ocular ultrasonography of the right eye showed a small globe (axial length 13.3 mm), vitreous cavity filled with moderately reflective dot echoes, gross choroidal thickening (3.0 mm), and no intraocular calcification, mass, or foreign body.
objective.advanced_workup: Orbital CT showed a shrunken right globe with hyperdense vitreous and no calcification. Following right eye enucleation (globe 12 x 13 x 12 mm), histopathology demonstrated a shrunken globe with scleral thickening, limbal lymphohistiocytic infiltration, dense iris infiltration by lymphocytes, plasma cells, and histiocytes, a shrunken cataractous lens with ruptured folded capsule, destroyed retina, and extensive granulomatous vitritis with Langerhans giant cells. Gomori methenamine silver (GMS) staining revealed multiple septate fungal hyphae, and ITS PCR-RFLP with HaeIII digestion identified Aspergillus fumigatus.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Endogenous right eye Aspergillus fumigatus granulomatous endophthalmitis in an immunocompetent 8-month-old infant, definitively confirmed by enucleation histopathology (GMS stain showing septate hyphae within granulomatous vitritis) and ITS rDNA PCR-RFLP identifying A. fumigatus, with retinoblastoma ruled out. Treated with right eye enucleation due to absent visual potential and phthisis; systemic evaluation showed no extraocular dissemination, and the child remained healthy at 6-month follow-up.
